title: Looking for builders!
author: Junior_Air_3329
selftext:
Howdy y’all. I was gonna post in the indie game dev sub, but I figured I’d be able to get the job done for a reasonable price here, and faster. 

I’m looking for a person or people who would be able to help me turn my game idea into a reality. I’ve been having ideas about this game just about my whole life, but since I don’t know code, (and nobody is willing to to teach me nuances and stuff around my learning disability) It never came to fruition.

So I just have loads and loads and loads of notes about mechanics and how the game should be…

But no way to implement it…

It’s got a lot to it, so I’m that aspect I’d say it’s a big game and I’m not sure how big ai can go.

I’d like it to be SUPER optimized but I understand ai probably isn’t there yet…

Honestly, I wouldn’t care who made it or if I got any credit as long as I got creative liberty and actually got to play it. 

😭😭😭

I want it to be online multiplayer..

Uhh dm me if interested? I dont know

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body: I promise it’s not that complicated, there is no prompting magic it just takes time,  dedication and a vision. Do you have a PC? Claude code will literally do it all for you. Set up a git hub and prompt away. Honestly while it’s easy if you want I can help you with everything I know but I promise it will literally just be downloading the Claude app, going setting up a git hub and prompting away. BUT I would actually do some planning with Claude first. I’d say just try a month of Claude and maybe instead of starting with your actual game idea come up with one you’re less passionate about, try your best and identify the problems that come up. Some common challenges people have involve assets and audio but neither hard to over come. It may take you a lot of time if you have a proper deep vision but I promise Claude’s the way to go,  and I promise it’ll be difficult to get other people to do it for you without significant compensation. But if you want to get a Claude sub I can help you with the teeny tiny bit I know. I started with an asset builder myself but that’s a difficult approach

replies.author: je386
replies.body:
You want multiplatform,  so you could use a game engine like godot or unity, but also kotlin multiplatform with compose multiplatform is an option (that supports not only android and iOS, but also web and desktop).

I would recommend learning the essentials of git first, select an engine or language and then start on a small project first.

When you start, you will make mistakes and errors, thats normal, but you want to learn on a small project you can set aside before starting with your dream project.

comments.author: FrozenFirebat
comments.body:
Start with the grand picture. what genre does the game sit in. Is it a subgenre of something, does it mix genres (usually mixing more than 2-3 starts to hurt you rather than help). How would you describe it in the format of "It's X, but with Y" (you can grow more unique features, but the hook has to be something concrete). Describe the main game loop. Once you do that, the game should come easily. A collection of mechanics or lore doesn't help you because some of them might not pair well, and they all need to fuel the main vision, so that's what you should focus on.

  
Also, AI can optimize. It helps if you know how to optimize and strategize with the AI on how to do it (because it forgets that it knows things).

Honestly, my advice to anybody new to game dev is to keep it single player, make it mechanic or narrative heavy instead of visually heavy. Try a unique twist to something already done before. The more original the concept, the harder of a time AI will have with producing it.

replies.author: FrozenFirebat
replies.body:
Extraction pvp game with an overhead arpg style, that's low poly. Not insane.

Start with making two prototypes. One that just let's you try out the combat on a training dummy and another that builds level features. Then when you feel comfortable, do multi-player. It would need to be server authoritative with rollback.

replies.author: FrozenFirebat
replies.body:
add your systems one at a time and rebalance (Ai is pretty good at designing automated tests). The one thing AI can't do is balance players, so you'll want it to build int some telemetry to grab gameplay data from play testers to help tune the game.

Also, this means you'll need to set up a cloud service (AI can help with that too). There are cheap options that range from Free (oracle) to $5/month (you wouldn't need more unless you have a mega hit and then you should be able to afford more). The free options aren't that reliable however.
